handoff: Blocking F1: --rebase-merges only fixes gh-80 while the story branch has not moved. If the story branch advances before integrate runs again, the merge is re-created and the same conflict comes back (repro in findings). Standards clean, tests and typecheck green.

findings.title: The resolution is lost again when the story branch advances after the merge step
findings.detail:
story.md Wanted: "A conflict resolved once in `merge` stays resolved when the workflow returns to `integrate`". That holds only when the story tip is unchanged. Repro in plain git 2.50: base commit with a.txt and b.txt; S and L change a.txt differently; on L, `git merge --no-ff S`, resolve to 'both', commit. Then commit an unrelated change to b.txt on S. `git rebase --rebase-merges S` on L stops with `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in a.txt` / `Could not apply <sha>... onto # resolve`: the same conflict on the same file. Without that extra commit on S it is a no-op, which is what the new test checks. A plain `git merge S` into L in the same state is clean. In the gh-75 incident other slices of the same story may integrate during the minutes the merge step runs, so this is the case most likely to repeat.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Make integrate never redo a merge the slice already made. For example, when the slice HEAD already contains a merge of the story branch (`git.isAncestor` of an earlier story tip through a merge, or simply any merge commit in story..slice), bring the story branch in with `git merge` instead of rebasing, then fast-forward. Or take the story's second direction: the merge step rebases, and `norn done` refuses until the slice is linear on top of the story tip. Add a regression test where the story branch gets an unrelated commit between the merge step and the second integrate.
